## Critique
- claim-1: The list and degrees are correct in the reduced grading \(\deg s_\lambda=|\lambda|\), but that grading, the ambient integral ring, the meaning of \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\), and the convention for classes outside the box are not explicitly defined. Strict standalone compliance also requires checking that \(x_1,y_1,x_2,z,y_2\) always lie in the box.
- claim-2: The boundary conditions are correct and exhaustive. It should explicitly say that \(0\) denotes the zero class, so \(\gamma\) or \(\theta\) is a named slot rather than a Schur class when omitted.
- claim-3: The identities are mathematically correct under integral Pieri multiplication, but the proof does not explicitly define \(h_1=s_{(1)}\), \(h_2=s_{(2)}\), enumerate all allowable one-box/horizontal-two-strip extensions, or explain why no others occur.
- claim-4: Substantively justified, but strict standalone establishment is premature until the preceding definitions and finite Pieri enumeration are supplied. No parent-theorem issue arises.

## Repair certificates
- [proof-attempt] State an ambient graded integral Schur/Pieri ring with basis \(\{s_\lambda:\lambda\subseteq q^r\}\), conventions \(\deg s_\lambda=|\lambda|\), \(h_1=s_{(1)}\), \(h_2=s_{(2)}\), and \(s_\lambda=0\) outside \(q^r\). Then verify box membership for every named partition and enumerate exactly the Pieri extensions yielding the four displayed identities, including all three cases \((p,c)=(1,1)\), \(p=1,c\ge2\), and \(p\ge2,c=1\).

## Required revisions
- Add the ambient-ring, box, grading, and zero-class conventions.
- Supply the finite box-membership and Pieri enumeration.
- Conclude only that this conditional standalone-restatement certificate is established.
